content.title: About
content.content: The orange is a citrus fruit native to Southeast Asia, now cultivated in warm regions worldwide. Its juicy, sweet‑tart flavor and fragrant aroma make it popular fresh and in many culinary applications.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oranges belong to the Rutaceae family and are hybrids of pomelo and mandarin.
The term “orange” was introduced to the United States in the 19th century, while in Russia the fruit was called “апельсин” only in the 20th century.
Orange peel is rich in essential oils used for flavorings and perfumes.
There are over 600 orange varieties, differing in taste, pulp color, and size.
Orange juice is a common source of vitamin C in dietary supplements.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: One medium orange provides more than 100 % of the daily vitamin C requirement, supporting immunity and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids such as hesperidin help improve vascular function and reduce inflammation.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: The fiber in oranges aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Supports skin health
items.content: Vitamin C is essential for collagen synthesis, helping maintain skin elasticity.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium assists in regulating fluid balance and maintaining normal blood pressure.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to citrus fruits, manifested as skin itching or swelling.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcer disease.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Orange juice can increase the effect of certain medications, such as statins, by influencing liver enzymes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Oranges can be eaten fresh, juiced, added to salads, desserts, smoothies, and marinades. For a milder taste, slice the segments and lightly roast them in the oven.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store oranges in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer, where they stay fresh for 2‑3 weeks. At room temperature they quickly lose aroma and become soft.
